findings.evidence: "updates the reimbursement log at the start of the fiscal year" ... "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral transition (e.g., "Separately") or correct the cadence so both statements actually align.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies the two update cadences match, but one happens once a year and the other happens monthly - the transition word misstates the relationship between the two facts.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific clock being referenced (e.g., "the 90-day eligibility period" or "the benefit-year claim window") instead of the vague phrase "stipend clock."
findings.location: Eligibility, paragraph on leave of absence
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the benefit-year claim window, or something else.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days." ... "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Specify consistent units for both figures, e.g., "three business days," and clarify what the three-day clock starts from.
findings.violation: The document mixes "business days" and plain "days" without clarifying whether the three-day reminder window uses the same unit, making the overall timeline impossible to compute reliably.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Enumerate the exception cases explicitly (e.g., purchases over a dollar threshold) or state that a photo is always sufficient.
findings.violation: "Most requests" is vague and doesn't tell the reader which requests require something more than a photo receipt.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence shifts to second-person ("you"/"we") while every other section uses third person ("employees," "the benefits team"), breaking the document's voice and leaving "we" undefined.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee" vs. Eligibility's "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year."
findings.fix: Clarify explicitly whether a claim can include multiple categories/devices or whether each category requires a separate claim.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions, second paragraph, compared with Eligibility
findings.violation: It's unclear whether "one claim per benefit year" means a single claim covering multiple device categories, or whether multiple claims are allowed as long as each stays within one device per category - the two rules aren't reconciled.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item... Finance reconciles the stipend item... Payroll releases the stipend item amount"
findings.fix: Vary the phrasing with pronouns/synonyms, and reconcile who actually disburses funds - Payroll, Finance, or the finance office - into one consistent description.
findings.violation: The phrase "stipend item" is repeated three times in three consecutive sentences, and this paragraph introduces "Payroll" as the payer, contradicting Reimbursement Amounts' statement that "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle."

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: State a single, consistent end-to-end timeline from submission to payment, or explain how the monthly reconciliation fits within that timeline.
findings.violation: A monthly reconciliation cadence is inconsistent with the two-business-day manager review (Approval Timeline) and the one-pay-cycle deposit (Reimbursement Amounts), leaving the real end-to-end timeline undefined.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Delete this paragraph or merge its content into the "How to Apply" section using third-person phrasing.
findings.violation: This duplicates information already given in "How to Apply" and switches back to second-person voice, making it redundant and inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite this section to match the step order in "How to Apply," and clarify that the receipt is uploaded after purchase, as part of the reimbursement claim.
findings.violation: This contradicts the fuller process described in "How to Apply" (start request, auto-saved draft, review confirmation summary, submit) and implies a receipt is uploaded before purchase/approval, which doesn't fit a reimbursement model.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Decide on one owner and one update cadence for the equipment catalog and use it consistently everywhere it's mentioned.
findings.violation: This contradicts Program Overview's statement that "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" - two different owners and two different cadences for the same catalog.

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Identify a single party responsible for disbursing payment and remove or correct the conflicting statements.
findings.violation: This conflicts with Reimbursement Amounts ("The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle") and Terminology Notes ("Payroll releases the stipend item amount"), giving three different parties responsible for the actual payment.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Add this review step into the Approval Timeline section and specify its effect on the overall turnaround time.
findings.violation: This additional review step isn't integrated into the Approval Timeline (manager review within two business days), leaving it unclear whether it happens before, after, or concurrently with that review, and whether it affects the stated timeline.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Either remove this check as redundant, or clarify a scenario (e.g., multi-item claims) under which repeat requests within a quarter are legitimately possible.
findings.violation: This contradicts Eligibility's rule that the stipend covers "one claim per employee per benefit year" - if only one claim per year is permitted, a quarterly-repeat flag is checking for something that should already be impossible.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Consolidate all equipment-catalog ownership/cadence statements into one consistent fact stated once.
findings.violation: This is a third conflicting claim about who maintains the equipment catalog and when, alongside the IT asset group (monthly, Program Overview) and the finance liaison (start of fiscal year, Special Cases).
